title: Lifting compatible maps through the completed proper pushforward comparison
statement: Let Y be a Noetherian scheme, J a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, and f:X\to Y a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let G be a coherent J-adic formal system and F a coherent module on X [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, pqf-def-coherent], and assume H=f_*F is coherent. Let kappa:H^\wedge\to(f_*(F/(J\mathcal O_X)^{n+1}F))_n be a morphism of inverse systems satisfying pi^J_n kappa_n=f_*(pi^I_n) for every n>=0, where pi^J_n and pi^I_n are the quotient projections. For any morphism of inverse systems gamma:G\to(f_*(F/(J\mathcal O_X)^{n+1}F))_n there exists a morphism alpha:G\to H^\wedge in the category of coherent formal modules such that alpha kappa=gamma. Only the lift through a supplied kappa is asserted; neither kappa nor gamma is constructed here.

source.place: Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull), first half of proof, construction of alpha from lim gamma; checked against https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/088B

proof.text: On each affine open V = Spec A in Y restrict f and F. Properness and coherence are preserved. Set I = J(V) and M = Gamma(V,f_*F). The affine ideal-product and quotient formulas identify the sections of the source of kappa with M/I^(n+1)M. The equations imposed on kappa identify its section maps with the canonical degree-zero formal-functions maps. The theorem on formal functions therefore identifies lim kappa with the canonical isomorphism from the I-adic completion of M to lim Gamma(f^(-1)V,F/I^(n+1)F).

The affine coherent-formal-module equivalence identifies G on V with the finite completed A-module N = lim Gamma(V,G_n), with surjective projections of kernel I^(n+1)N. Compose lim gamma with the inverse of lim kappa to obtain a map N to the completion of M. It is linear over the completed ring: reduce each scalar to A/I^(n+1); every gamma_n is A-linear and each target term is killed by I^(n+1), so the scalar equality holds after every limit projection, hence in the limit. This map descends to N/I^(n+1)N -> M/I^(n+1)M. The affine tilde/sections equivalence supplies the component sheaf maps alpha_n. The descending maps commute with transitions by their construction from one map on limits, so they form a coherent-formal-module morphism. After precomposition with the surjective projection N -> Gamma(V,G_n), the equation alpha_n kappa_n = gamma_n is exactly the definition of the map on limits; cancellation proves it.

If two local alpha maps have alpha kappa = gamma, their maps on limits agree because lim kappa is invertible. Surjectivity of the projections from N proves equality at each level; the affine tilde/sections equivalence proves equality of their sheaf maps. Restriction to smaller affine opens preserves completion quotients and all the asserted equations. Local uniqueness therefore identifies restrictions. On overlaps cover by smaller affine opens rather than assuming intersections affine. Glue the local sheaf morphisms at each level; their transition identities and alpha kappa = gamma are checked on the affine basis and therefore hold globally. This gives the required global alpha. Zero ideals give constant systems and unit ideals zero systems, and the same construction applies to zero modules and empty affine opens.

lean.statement:
theorem formalCompletion_pushforward_lift {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y]
    (J : Y.IdealSheafData) (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    (G : CoherentFormalModule Y J) (F : CoherentModules X)
    (h : RingedSpace.IsCoherent Y.toRingedSpace
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F.obj))
    (κ : formalCompletionSystem J ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F.obj) ⟶
      formalCompletionSystem (J.comap f) F.obj ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward f)
    (hκ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      formalModuleQuotientπ J (n + 1) ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F.obj) ≫
        κ.app (op n) = (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).map
          (formalModuleQuotientπ (J.comap f) (n + 1) F.obj))
    (γ : G.obj ⟶ formalCompletionSystem (J.comap f) F.obj ⋙
      Scheme.Modules.pushforward f) :
    ∃ α : G ⟶ (completion Y J).obj
        ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F.obj, h⟩,
      α.hom ≫ κ = γ
